title: Hilbert-Schmidt Lipschitz bridge for the capped Liouvillian kernel
question: Can the unit scalar Lipschitz bound for the capped Matsubara kernel be lifted to a gap-free Hilbert-Schmidt functional-calculus comparison of finite Liouvillians, thereby isolating eigenvector rotation from spatial locality?
method: Build the exact cutoff-2 V=2 edge doubled-bond commutator Liouvillian and perturb it with a noncommuting onsite momentum term.
Apply the exact capped functional calculus and the 64-term positive odd-Matsubara partial functional calculus at beta=1/2 and beta=1.
Measure Frobenius differences against the Liouvillian perturbation, check positivity and Hermiticity, and link the source R-375 run with its 2816 all-prefix context count.
Reconstruct the calculation with the independent R-372 helper and compile Lean R376 for scalar absolute-value nonexpansiveness.
finding: The primary and independent lanes pass the finite noncommuting stress. The largest full-kernel Hilbert-Schmidt ratio is 0.9787544362168733, the largest 64-layer partial ratio is 0.9755896836319287, the commutator Frobenius norm is 2.5999999999999983, and the integrated verifier passes 76/76 with Lean R376 PASS.
decision_reason: The finite Schatten-2 functional-calculus stress supports a gap-free eigenvector-rotation interface: the observed ratios stay below the unit scalar budget without dividing by a spectral gap. It remains a small finite test, not a proof of the general theorem or of spatial locality, so no promotion is justified.

The perturbation might commute with the selected bond and fail to test eigenvector rotation.
The comparison might hide an inverse minimum-gap factor.
The absolute-value cusp could invalidate a derivative-based argument.
The finite odd-frequency budget could exceed one or the partial matrix ratio could exceed it.
Cutoff 2 at one volume could hide cutoff or volume growth.
Functional calculus of the finite Liouvillian might not equal the full weighted Q3 shell.
The independent lane might import the primary implementation.
The finite interface might silently close common alpha, C6 or Pre-A.

next_action: Establish the general Schatten-2 functional-calculus lemma for the capped kernel, then combine it with an energy-constrained local commutator estimate on the common polynomial core.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite small-edge Liouvillian Hilbert-Schmidt checkpoint only. It does not prove an operator-norm bound, spatial locality, common core, common alpha, KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A.
no_overclaim: R-376 isolates a finite eigenvector-rotation interface but does not prove the general operator theorem or any QFT closure.
